paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. Jesus doesn't hand the disciples a date. He hands them a warning: "See to it that no one deceives you." (Matthew 24:4) He says it, then says it again about the false prophets (Matthew 24:11), so I wrote it on my apron in BIG letters.

Then Jesus tells them the wars, famines and earthquakes are "the beginning of birth pains." (Matthew 24:8) The BEGINNING, friend. So when the news gets loud, they're not to be alarmed, because "the end is still to come." (Matthew 24:6) Jesus also says "the love of most will grow cold," (Matthew 24:12) and I think that's the part to hold up to your own heart, so stay close to the oven and keep it warm.

Here's the good news, and I'm saying it LOUD: "the one who perseveres to the end will be saved." (Matthew 24:13) Jesus says this gospel "will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations," (Matthew 24:14) and you and I get to be part of that. Nobody knows the day or the hour (Matthew 24:36), so my job is to keep the ovens ready, and yours is to keep trusting Jesus and keep loving. The story isn't over, because Jesus is still sitting on that mountain teaching.
